message.text:
**Computing fan-in robustly**

I’m thinking about how to compute the fan-in effectively. A Perl script could help with declarations for production, but I want to exclude tests and count occurrences globally while avoiding name collisions. Candidates like `ValidateContent`, `RenderMarkdown`, and others come to mind. I can use a Perl script to analyze file lists and regex for counts without file operations. I need to focus on exported methods and ensure I handle common name collisions thoughtfully.

args.command:
perl -e '
@files=`find . -type f -name "*.go" 2>/dev/null`; chomp @files; my %decl; for $f (@files){ next if $f !~ m{^\./internal/}; next if $f =~ /_test\.go$/; open F,"<",$f or next; while(<F>){ if(/^func\s+(?:\([^)]*\)\s*)?([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(/){$decl{$1}{$f}=1} } close F } for $n (keys %decl){my $c=0; for $f (@files){next if $f =~ /_test\.go$/; open F,"<",$f or next; while(<F>){$c += () = /\b\Q$n\E\b/g} close F} my $d=scalar keys %{$decl{$n}}; $c-=$d; print "$c\t$n\t",join(",",keys %{$decl{$n}}),"\n" }' | sort -rn | awk 'NR<=40 {print}'
